### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**15** anchor(s) derived from **4** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b2c458f7d17516a714b02de8b4ac13de7952d8af` — the merge of head `924c58ca4d7fa6b08439d4aee327a1845600b47d` into base `69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b2c458f7d17516a714b02de8b4ac13de7952d8af && git checkout b2c458f7d17516a714b02de8b4ac13de7952d8af
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4 924c58ca4d7fa6b08439d4aee327a1845600b47d && git checkout -B drift-repro 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4 && git merge --no-ff 924c58ca4d7fa6b08439d4aee327a1845600b47d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 69301483be2bae6ff1dcbd156b3c04c062dd92e4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a3a3ae8e8feb98b8116401cf81a6d9aa2afb5314`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-package-scope.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts, .changeset/32071-pull-reads-mapping-by-job-package.md, content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx (prose, judged for accuracy) + read, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/core/src/artifact-packages.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-resolver.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (packageScopedHoldersOf, getPackageScopedItem, getEnvironmentScopedItem, overlaySlotBinding, isPackageDisabled), packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (recordResidualOwner), packages/metadata-core/src/package-closure.ts (packageResolutionClosure), packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts + protocol-meta-item-reads.ts + protocol-meta-item-face.ts + protocol-authoring-refusals.ts, packages/runtime/src/artifact-collections.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts (collectBundleJobs, the kernel:ready schedule), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (disable door), packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts (bindArtifactHandlers), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (pullConnectorSource), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/package-scoped-declarations.ts (listedHoldersView), scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs, docs/adr/0150 D3/D5, docs/adr/0005

Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts): success on Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, Check PR Size, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Dogfood Regression Gate, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, the three Lint · scoped runs, Type Check · source gates, both Plan shards, filter, Auto Label. PENDING at read time: Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check UI, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16. No failure. The dev's local counts are not a gate verdict; Test Core is the one that decides the pins and it has not answered.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Binder passes the declaring package: right.** `jobDeclaringPackages` walks `resolveArtifactPackageOrder`. A body's job answers that body by identity, a top-level copy answers by name, and a single-package artifact answers `appId`. This matches ruling Q1 and carrier point 2. It adds no new throw: `collectBundleJobs` already runs the same resolver on the same bundle earlier in `scheduleAppArtifactJobs`. Only array-form jobs are scheduled, so the `Array.isArray` guard loses nothing.
- **The pull reads own, then the closure's one holder plus `sys`, then refuses: right against D3.** `mappingNameResolver` calls `resolvePackageScopedName(registry, { type: 'mapping', name, callerPackageId })` at question time, so a dependency added later is seen. It does not use `getMetaItem({ packageId })`, which is correct: that is the D5 exact qualifier and would refuse a closure holder (ruling Q2).
- **Refusal shape: right.** `code` and `status` are read off `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT` / 409), the sentence is the resolver's, and the reason is Part A's `mapping_name_refused`. No code is minted and no literal is written (ADR-0112). The refusal happens before the connector call and before any write, pinned for D3 (c).
- **Sibling body with no dependency is refused `outside-closure`: right.** This is ADR-0150 D3 (c) and its N1 note ("a sibling package of the same release artifact is no exception"). It is declared.
- **No-package caller: unchanged.** Absent, `null` and `''` take Part A's protocol read, pinned over the three values. A composition with no registry falls back to the same read, as the spec TSDoc says an older implementation does.
- **Dev flag 1 (environment row under a package mapping's name): confirmed; it need not be declared as a move.** `overlaySlotBinding` binds a package-less bare-slot row to the one composite holder, so `getPackageScopedItem(holder)` returns the row and `getEnvironmentScopedItem` returns nothing. With one holder, both callers get the row, as before. With two holders the row binds to neither: the package caller gets its own composite item and the no-package caller is refused, also as before. The changeset's CONTROL sentence is accurate. One process gap: the Part B ruling 6770706358 still lists this as a move to declare, and no amendment withdraws it.
- **Carrier item 3: discharged.** The `callerPackageId` TSDoc no longer says "exactly as today", states the D3 no-package read, and the doc pin refuses the old phrase.
- **Wrong: a disabled package's mapping is now pulled** (must-fix 1 in ④).
- **Wrong: a residual top-level job is a package caller with no closure** (must-fix 2 in ④).

### ② Semver level

- **Level: `patch` on runtime, service-automation and spec is correct.** Under AGENTS.md the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone, and a breaking non-protocol change ships `patch` with its BREAKING banner.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` is correct.** No schema, key, accepted value or published shape moves; the spec change is TSDoc plus its pin. This matches the D3 (c) precedents (.changeset/31790, 31741, 31853, and Part A).
- **Mechanics hold.** Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. The changeset carries one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), which fits. The BREAKING item carries its FROM, TO and one-line fix. The "Supersedes, in the same release" line correctly retires Part A's "does not yet read `callerPackageId`".
- **FROM→TO is incomplete: must-fix.** Two moved answers are missing (④ items 1 and 2). First-party count for both is 0, since no first-party package declares a job `pull`; that does not excuse the declaration.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` contradicts the PR's own text: should-fix, for the seat to rule.** The body calls move 1 "A widening" (409 to served), and the diff adds two optional members to published types exported from the service-automation root (`ConnectorPullOptions.callerPackageId`, `ConnectorPullDeps.mappingByPackage`). `clause2-line.mjs` names this combination: `yes (narrowing)`, "a diff that widens one surface and narrows another". The 31790 changeset spelled the mixed case `yes (widening); narrowing ... declared below`. Either restate the line in the PR body and changeset, or record why `no` stands (move 1 only undoes Part A's unreleased 409). The level does not change either way.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Flag 1, env-overlay control: answered.** Confirmed in ①; no declaration owed. The seat should amend the ruling's fourth bullet.
- **Flag 2, `jobs.mdx` outside the ruled surface: the edit is justified but not fully accurate (should-fix).** Part A's sentence "a pull cannot yet read its own package's mapping" became false with this diff, so leaving it would ship a false doc. Two inaccuracies remain:
  - "the package body the job sits in, not the artifact's top-level id" is false for a top-level job no body declares; the code and the changeset send exactly the top-level id.
  - "declare the dependency" is not available to that residual caller (④ item 2).
  - Smaller: the reach is the transitive closure, not only the declared `dependencies`.
- **Flag 3, objectql `package-scoped-read.ts` module doc: a carry, not a must-fix here.** It still says the connector pull reads "with no package", which is now false for every job pull. The file is outside the diff and the ruled surface, and changes no behaviour. But the PR says `Fixes #32071` and the report says "carrier: domain:server#3 · not filed", so the carry has no home once the card closes. Should-fix: file it before merge, or take the two-line doc edit in the fix round.
- **Escalation to the epic seat.** Must-fix 1 needs a ruling on which reader class the pull is: an API reader that stops on disable, or a resolution reader that keeps serving. Must-fix 2 needs a ruling on whether a residual owner, which `ObjectQL#recordResidualOwner` says "is not a package", is a package caller at all.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing does make the spec's own refusal real: `ConnectorSourcePullRequest.callerPackageId` already promised own, then closure, then refusal, and D3 (c) is the ruled rule. The must-fixes are in what the new read path dropped and in what the declaration leaves out.

1. **must-fix — a disabled package's mapping moves from refused to pulled; undeclared, unpinned.**
   - **Before (main a2bdaea1):** every pull read `protocol.getMetaItem({ type: 'mapping', name })`, the served face. `readMetaItemFace` withholds an item whose `_packageId` is a disabled package (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`, #24210, pinned in `package-disable-enforcement.test.ts`: "a disabled package's item is answered as a missing name is, on every type"). The pull then answered `404 MAPPING_NOT_FOUND`.
   - **After:** every job pull carries a package and reads `resolvePackageScopedName` over the raw registry. `packageScopedHoldersOf` is documented as unfiltered by disable, and `getPackageScopedItem` does not ask `isPackageDisabled`.
   - **Reach:** nothing cancels or gates jobs on disable. The disable door (`runtime/src/domains/packages.ts`) only calls `registry.disablePackage`, and neither `scheduleAppArtifactJobs` nor the job service asks `isPackageDisabled`. So the armed pull job of a disabled package, or of an enabled package whose closure holder is disabled, now calls the upstream connector and writes rows through a mapping the platform answers as absent everywhere else. This covers the common single-package case too.
   - **Fix:** withhold a disabled holder's item on the package-caller path so it answers `mapping_not_found` as before (plugin-sharing's `listedHoldersView` is the existing precedent for this resolver), with a pin for an own-disabled and a closure-holder-disabled case. Or declare the move with a ruling.
   - **Confidence:** read off the code, not run.
   - **Related:** the two paths are now two readers. The no-package read is the protocol's (store row, conversion, withholding); the package read is the registry's. Their agreement is pinned only inside one `SchemaRegistry`.

2. **must-fix — a residual top-level job's cross-body pull moves from pulled to refused; undeclared, and the stated remedy does not exist.**
   - **What happens:** in a multi-package artifact whose top-level id is not also a body's id, `jobDeclaringPackages` returns `appId` for a job no body declares. That id has no package row. `packageResolutionClosure` says of such a caller: "a caller package the registry cannot produce declares nothing, so it reaches `sys` only". `judgeJobPull` binds the job when any body declares the mapping.
   - **Result:** the job arms and every run is refused `outside-closure`; on main it pulled. The mirror case is the same: a body's job pulling a mapping filed under the residual owner.
   - **Declaration gap:** the `Narrowing:` line and changeset item 2 cover only "a job in one package body pulling a mapping only another body ... declares". The remedy in the refusal sentence, the changeset and `jobs.mdx` ("declare the dependency") cannot be applied by a non-package; only "move the job or mapping into one package" works.
   - **Fix:** declare this FROM→TO with a truthful fix, and pin it at the resolver over a real registry (today the residual case is pinned only as the return value of `jobDeclaringPackages`). Or have the seat rule that a residual owner reads as a caller with no package.

3. **should-fix — the `Clause-②` line** (②).
4. **should-fix — the two `jobs.mdx` inaccuracies** (③ flag 2).
5. **should-fix — file the objectql module-doc carry before the card closes** (③ flag 3).
6. **nit — stale comments in diff files.** The `connector-pull.ts` module header step 1 still says the mapping is read "through the protocol's `getMetaItem`". The `mapping_name_refused` TSDoc omits the environment-only holder (D3 (a)). The `connector-package-scope.ts` module header speaks only of connectors.
7. **nit — sentinel caller ids.** A `callerPackageId` of `sys_metadata` or `__runtime__` is treated as a package by the pull's guard but as no package by the resolver, so that no-package read goes through the registry and not the protocol. No binder sends either value.
8. **nit — a D3 refusal is deterministic, yet the run is `failed` and the `retryPolicy` retries it.** Same as Part A.

Break attempts that held:
- A-job with B-mapping and a dependency is pulled; without one it is refused naming B.
- Two holders in the closure are refused `ambiguous-in-closure`.
- Own plus another holder serves own.
- A `sys` holder is in every reach.
- A package-less environment mapping is served to a no-package caller and refused to a package caller (D3 (a)); it is pinned and correctly described as unreachable through the binder.
- After the holder is uninstalled the name is not-found (404), and an uninstalled app's jobs are retired by the existing cleanup.
- The reason string and envelope match Part A.
- No pin claims to iterate a live set; the spec doc pin reads the source text, and the no-package CONTROL loops the three absent spellings.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dfc7a7def4b5ce16724cd9b6d2e733c508127b17`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.ts, packages/runtime/src/app-artifact-handlers.job-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-package-scope.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts (module doc), .changeset/32071-pull-reads-mapping-by-job-package.md, content/docs/automation/jobs.mdx (prose, judged for accuracy)

Second round. The first-round record is comment 6773340046 (FAIL on `a3a3ae8e`). This one is judged against the seat's fix-round rulings (card #32071 comment 6773359878) and the dev's fix-round report (6775712900). Read, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-refusals.ts (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, and on `origin/main` `121640b9` packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts and connector-pull.ts.

Check-runs on the head (the gate verdicts), read at 18:54Z: every non-skipped run is `success`, none pending, none failed. That covers Build Core, Test Core 1/8 to 8/8 and its roll-up, all five Type Check runs, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Build & E2E UI, Live E2E UI, Build Docs, every Lint run, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness and Dogfood Regression Gate. Test Core (3/8) is `success` here; it was the one failure on `a3a3ae8e` (the `seed-tenancy-autonumber-split` 5 s timeout the dev reported, on a path outside this diff), so that timeout did not recur. The PR itself reads `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty` (④ item 1).

### ① Derived judgments

- **Must-fix 1 (disabled package's mapping): closed.**
  - `mappingNameResolver` now passes the resolution through `withholdDisabledHolder`. A resolution to a disabled package holder (own, or the one closure holder) becomes `not-found`, as does an `outside-closure` refusal whose single candidate is a disabled package. The pull then answers `404 MAPPING_NOT_FOUND` / `mapping_not_found` through the existing not-found branch, before any call or write.
  - The predicate is live in production: `packageScopedRegistryOf` returns the registry object itself, so `isPackageDisabled` is reachable on it.
  - Three pins cover own disabled, closure holder disabled (pulled again once re-enabled) and sole outside holder disabled. Each asserts the no-package answer beside it, through the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.getMetaItem`, so "as main answers" is measured in the test.
  - `packageScopedHoldersOf` is untouched, as ruled.
- **The deviation (withhold after resolution, not filter holders): accepted.** The ruling says both "the way `listedHoldersView` does" and "where a disabled holder sits beside an enabled one in the closure, today's refusal stays until #32183". A holder filter would break the second clause by resolving that pair to the enabled holder. Withholding after resolution keeps both, and it is the served face's own pattern (`isItemOfDisabledPackage` is applied to the resolved answer). The CONTROL pin shows the pair is still refused 409 naming both, on both paths. The extra `outside-closure` branch is needed: without it a sole disabled outside holder would move from 404 to 409.
- **Must-fix 2 (residual top-level job): closed.**
  - `jobDeclaringPackages` now returns `undefined` for a top-level job no body declares, unless a body carries the top-level id. The binder spreads `callerPackageId` only when defined, so that run takes the protocol read, as on main.
  - Pinned at the binder (the run's request has no `callerPackageId` key) and at the resolver over a real `SchemaRegistry` (a no-package pull reads a body's mapping, and a mapping filed under the top-level id).
- **Mirror case: reported as measured, and the report is right.** A body's job pulling a mapping filed under the top-level id is refused 409 `outside-closure` naming that id, where main pulled. The top-level id has no package row, so no closure can contain it. Pinned ("MIRROR").
- **Unchanged from round one and still right:** the binder's per-body id, the refusal's code, status and sentence taken from `PackageScopedNameRefusedError`, the no-package path over absent, `null` and `''`, and the no-registry fallback.
- **Fix commit and main merge broke nothing in scope.** The only files differing between `a3a3ae8e` and `dfc7a7de` inside the PR's surface are the eight the fix commit names. The merge of `7993aa76` brought no conflict resolution into them: `git diff 7993aa76 dfc7a7de` is exactly the PR's 11 files.

### ② Semver level

- **Level and `Metadata-protocol: none`: unchanged, correct.** `patch` on runtime, service-automation and spec. The spec change is still TSDoc plus its pin.
- **Should-fix 3 (`Clause-②` reason sentence): closed.** `no (narrowing)` stands by ruling. The sentence saying why is in the changeset and in the PR body ("Why `no`: ..."). Check Changeset and PR-body guards are green with it.
- **FROM→TO at the new head: complete for every pulled/refused move.**
  - Move 1, 409 → own item: declared.
  - Move 2, D3 (c), BREAKING: declared with its fix.
  - Move 3, the mirror, BREAKING: declared FROM pulled TO 409 `outside-closure` naming the top-level id. The fix is truthful and applicable: "declare the dependency" is correctly not offered, and both remedies work (move the mapping into the job's body; move the job to the top level, where the no-package read of the top-level mapping is pinned as pulled). The PR body's `Narrowing:` line carries it as item (2).
  - D3 (a): declared as unreachable through the binder.
  - Env-overlay: a CONTROL, by the withdrawn bullet.
- **One refusal-to-refusal move is not in the changeset: should-fix.** A job whose own package is disabled, with a second enabled holder of the same name: main answers `409 mapping_name_refused` (two holders, Part A), this head answers `404 mapping_not_found` (own resolved, then withheld). The dev names it under `side_effects_noted` in the report only. Nothing is pulled either way and Part A's 409 is unreleased, so one sentence in the changeset is enough.
- **`packages/objectql` carries a doc-only edit and no changeset entry.** Check Changeset passes, so the gate accepts it; no action.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Should-fix 4 (`jobs.mdx`): closed.** The paragraph now says a top-level job no body declares reads with no package, the reach is transitive ("directly or through their own dependencies, and `sys`"), "declare a dependency" is offered only when the holder is another package, and a top-level holder gets the two remedies that work. The disabled sentence matches the code, including its "when it is the one the job would read" qualifier.
- **Should-fix 5 (objectql `package-scoped-read.ts` module doc): closed.** It now says only a pull that names no package reads through the protocol, and a pull naming its package reads through `resolvePackageScopedName`. It is inside the amended file surface.
- **Nit 6: closed at this head.** The `connector-pull.ts` header step 1, the `mapping_name_refused` TSDoc (now including D3 (a)) and the `connector-package-scope.ts` header are all corrected. The TSDoc fix sits in the conflict hunk (④ item 1) and has to be re-homed.
- **Nits 7 and 8: kept by ruling,** and recorded in the os-dev-report and the PR body.
- **File surface: held.** The eight files of the fix round are all inside the surface as amended by 6773359878.

### ④ Design judgment

All first-round findings are closed, and the contract content of this head holds against ADR-0150 D3 and the fix-round rulings. The one blocking finding is new and comes from `main` moving after the head was cut.

1. **must-fix — the head does not merge into `main`.**
   - **Evidence:** GitHub reports `mergeable: false` / `dirty`. `git merge-tree origin/main dfc7a7de` (main at `121640b9`, 18 commits past the merged `7993aa76`) gives a content conflict in `packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts`.
   - **Cause:** #32275 (`0561e609`) moved `ConnectorPullRefusalReason` and `ConnectorPullError` out of `connector-pull.ts` into a new `pull-refusal.ts`. This PR edits the `mapping_name_refused` TSDoc in the old place.
   - **What the resolution must do:**
     - Carry the nit-6 TSDoc into `pull-refusal.ts`. On main that file still has the stale sentence ("more than one package holds it"), so taking main's side reopens nit 6.
